prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable living genetic biobank covers endangered species at the Main KPI of 44,000 species banked; coverage of the most threatened species is a small fraction. A 2026 gap analysis of the Millennium Seed Bank Partnership, the largest seed-banking network (101 countries, 52,874 taxa banked), found only 474 critically endangered taxa banked, about 7.21% of them, only 9.49% in sufficient numbers for restoration, 6,120 critically endangered taxa unbanked, and 11.6 to 17.2% of those needing non-seed methods because their seeds are desiccation-intolerant (https://doi.org/10.1007/s10531-025-03246-z). Animal biobanks hold cells and gametes from thousands of species, limited by sample availability and species-specific cryotolerance (https://doi.org/10.1262/jrd.2025-114); coral cryobanking reached 100 species (https://doi.org/10.3390/cells11172668). GitHub has no open biobank registry or coverage tool for endangered species. Honest limit: seed banking and cell cryopreservation protocols are known, so tasks that only bank more samples with existing protocols are not new work; the open, checkable pieces are protocols for desiccation-intolerant seeds and taxa with no working cryopreservation, and a verified species-level coverage analysis. The Frozen Zoo inventory page could not be retrieved (404), so its counts are not relied on.
